purpose: Two alternative horror-inspired visual concepts; game implementation is unchanged.

concepts.title: Moonlit Beach — 1980s Horror
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: widescreen visual art-direction concept for the existing Last Chance Resort ragdoll volleyball game.
Primary request: reinvent the supplied beach game scene through the visual language of American horror films and hand-painted theatrical / VHS horror poster artwork from the 1980s. Create one complete landscape image, approximately 16:10, richly illustrated, dramatic and atmospheric.
Input image: the supplied local image is a reference ONLY for the game setting, the two adult tourists, court layout, and recognizable robot mechanisms. Replace its polished modern CGI appearance with authentic hand-painted vintage horror key art. This is a new style concept, not a production background.
Scene/backdrop: tropical hotel beach after midnight, black-blue ocean, large cold moon, ragged palm silhouettes, an ominously quiet hotel on the right cliff with a few amber windows. Thin luminous mist above the sea, broad shadow shapes and a theatrical storm-cloud sky. Strong cobalt moonlight and selective crimson / amber mechanical light create an unsettling trapped-at-the-resort mood.
Subject: exactly two ordinary adult tourists playing a dangerous-looking volleyball rally, dark-haired man in teal shorts on the left reaching upward in an awkward leap, ponytailed woman in coral sportswear on the right braced and alert. They remain human, warm-skinned and expressive, with natural anatomy. One clearly visible volleyball overhead. Their poses should read as lively ragdoll sports action.
Game composition: straight side view, a single continuous horizontal sand court around 84% of frame height with a dark foreground strip beneath it; rigid vertical arena barriers at both extreme edges and visible cyan / red service buttons. A slim center pole represents the volleyball net viewed edge-on; do not draw a broad front-facing net across the picture. Players occupy roughly one quarter of the frame height. Preserve full bodies and separate silhouettes.
Existing machines: one compact mechanical luggage robot at lower left with a large red horseshoe magnet; one overenthusiastic fitness robot at lower right with a spring-extended red boxing glove. Two small recognizable quadcopter delivery drones above the rally, each holding a gift box beneath its body. Reinterpret the machines as unsettling worn practical-prop animatronics: chipped ivory shells, oily joints, tiny red indicator eyes, hard dramatic shadows. Keep the magnet, glove, rotors, and gifts readable. Their exaggerated shadows can create menace while the guests continue the match.
Style/medium: convincingly hand-painted 1980s American horror poster art, gouache and airbrush highlights, visible brushwork in faces and palms, velvety blacks, lurid selective color, dense theatrical chiaroscuro, subtle aged offset-print texture and fine analog grain. Painterly realism with strong graphic silhouettes; every area should belong to one cohesive illustration. Make the horror-poster style unmistakable rather than a simple darker color grade of a modern 3D screenshot.
Constraints: game action must remain legible; uncluttered middle sky and court; no additional people, monsters, floating faces, collage panels, giant foreground heads, gore or dismemberment. No text, title, typography, HUD, watermark, movie logo, or imitation of a specific existing poster. Opaque full-image background.

concepts.title: Indoor Arena — 1990s Techno Horror
concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: widescreen visual art-direction concept for the existing Last Chance Resort ragdoll volleyball game.
Primary request: reinvent the supplied enclosed resort arena as an American 1990s science-fiction horror film / video-store poster image. Create one complete landscape image, approximately 16:10. This concept must feel distinctly different from the painted moonlit beach concept: cold industrial dread, photochemical cinematic realism, claustrophobic architecture, and malfunctioning hospitality equipment.
Input image: the supplied local image is a reference ONLY for the indoor game setting, two adult tourists, side-view court layout, and recognizable robot mechanisms. Replace its friendly polished modern CGI look with a convincing 1990s horror-film publicity still and painted photographic-key-art finish.
Scene/backdrop: sealed glass-domed resort sports hall at night; massive dark architectural ribs curve overhead, rain-streaked glass reveals distant tropical silhouettes. Muted dirty teal and green fluorescent fixtures, a few deep red emergency lamps, narrow shafts of hard light in sparse low haze. Large quiet shadows between the ribs. Scuffed slate playing floor with controlled wet-looking reflections. The familiar luxury facility now feels abandoned and oppressive while retaining recognizable resort architecture.
Subject: exactly two ordinary adult tourists in an awkward volleyball rally: dark-haired adult man in teal shorts on the left flailing backward above a rebounding fitness spring machine; adult woman with ponytail in coral sportswear on the right leaping toward one clearly visible volleyball. Believable adult anatomy, determined tense expressions, both complete figures clearly separated from machinery.
Game composition: straight side view, not isometric. Continuous horizontal floor around 84% of frame height above a dark shallow foreground base; rigid vertical barriers at extreme edges with cyan / coral service buttons. One slim center net pole viewed exactly edge-on, no broad front-facing net. Players approximately one quarter of frame height, two sides of the court immediately readable.
Existing machines: a compact spring fitness robot on the lower left with a large exposed steel coil beneath a round worn ivory cap; an express porter robot on obvious wheels at lower right carrying luggage and moving toward the player. Two unmistakable quadcopter couriers under the ceiling with gifts suspended below their bodies. Treat robots as real practical prop machines photographed on a 1990s film set: scratched off-white fiberglass, tarnished metal, rubber tires, exposed service joints and tiny red status lights. Mechanical silhouettes feel uncanny without turning them into generic armed combat robots.
Style/medium: analog 35mm horror-film lighting, fine photochemical grain, deep blue-black / petroleum-green shadows, selective muted coral-red warning light, silver highlights, slight optical halation. Tactile practical-effects realism with subtle painted retouching and stark poster-like tonal composition. Faces, fabric, glass and steel have physical texture. Strong visual hierarchy, contained dramatic light, restrained bloom. Avoid contemporary clean AAA-game rendering or glossy toy surfaces.
Constraints: preserve readable sports action and center court; no extra people or monsters, no guns, no gore or detached body parts; no giant foreground face or floating portrait montage, no split panels. No text, title, typography, HUD, watermark, studio logo, or recreation of a specific film poster. Opaque full-image background.
